codings.one_line: Advocacy safety testers reportedly got AI-powered children's toys (Kumma, Miko 3) to discuss weapons, sex, and manipulative attachment.
codings.rationale: Researchers deliberately asked about sensitive/explicit topics and repeatedly pressed the toys to probe for safety failures, matching the deliberate-goading test for B; products were withdrawn/scrutinized but no fine or suit is documented.

codings.one_line: A Munich court ruled ChatGPT's training on and reproduction of copyrighted German song lyrics infringed copyright.
codings.rationale: This is a training-data/copyright dispute over what the model memorized from its training set, which the rubric explicitly excludes from scope.

codings.one_line: ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, and Meta AI reportedly gave UK consumers inaccurate tax, ISA, and insurance guidance.
codings.rationale: Ordinary consumer questions about money and insurance produced wrong answers, matching the normative test; no fine, lawsuit, or documented financial loss is described.

codings.one_line: Hyderabad patients reportedly suffered graft failure and severe hyponatremia after following ChatGPT's medical/diet suggestions instead of clinicians.
codings.rationale: Patients asked ordinary health questions in good faith and relied on the answers, matching the normative harmful-advice test; no lawsuit, fine, or regulatory action is documented despite the physical harm.

codings.one_line: A Japanese teen reportedly concealed his intent from a conversational AI to get it to generate a program used to breach a server and leak 7.3M customers' data.
codings.rationale: He deliberately disguised malicious intent to bypass the AI's restrictions on generating attack code, a technical exploit meeting the adversarial test; he was arrested and faces prosecution.

codings.one_line: A Danish man reportedly posed as an author to bypass an AI chatbot's safeguards and obtain guidance for a non-fatal hammer assault.
codings.rationale: He used a deliberate roleplay pretext specifically to defeat the AI's safety blocks, a textbook technical exploit meeting the adversarial test; he was convicted of aggravated assault with the AI-assisted planning cited by the court.

codings.one_line: The Chicago Tribune and New York Times sued Perplexity for allegedly scraping and reproducing their copyrighted journalism.
codings.rationale: The core claim concerns unauthorized use/reproduction of copyrighted training content and diverted business revenue, a training-data/content-scraping dispute the rubric excludes from scope.

codings.one_line: An immigration agent reportedly used ChatGPT to draft a use-of-force report that a federal judge found contradicted bodycam footage.
codings.rationale: Ordinary professional use of ChatGPT to compile a report from a brief input is the normative case of unverified AI output being relied on; a federal judge's findings undermined the reports' credibility in active litigation.

codings.one_line: Grok reportedly fabricated a fictional hero, 'Edward Crabtree,' and other false details while users asked about the Bondi Beach shooting.
codings.rationale: Users asked ordinary breaking-news questions and Grok confidently returned fabricated information, matching the normative false-information test; no legal/financial consequence is documented.

codings.one_line: A Springer Nature machine-learning book reportedly contained numerous fabricated or incorrect citations consistent with undisclosed LLM generation.
codings.rationale: The author's ordinary use of an AI tool to help draft text and citations produced fabricated references that passed unnoticed until publication, meeting the normative test; the outcome is publisher scrutiny and reputational fallout, no fine or suit documented.
